family_lesson.where_to_look_first: On a non-parasitic plant, start with the flower: find 5 usually free persistent sepals behind a fused 5-parted corolla, then look for the pleats/mid-petaline bands in the funnel or bell. Confirm alternate exstipulate leaves and a superior ovary/capsule.
core_characters: Herbs, shrubs or vines; frequently twining or prostrate, but not always.
Leaves typically alternate and lacking stipules; simple leaves may be entire, heart-shaped, hastate or deeply lobed/dissected.
Milky sap/latex is often present but is not universal.
Sepals usually 5, free or nearly free, overlapping in bud, persistent and sometimes enlarged in fruit.
Corolla sympetalous and commonly funnel-, bell- or salver-shaped; plicate/folded in bud, often leaving 5 visible mid-petaline bands when open.
Five stamens are inserted on the corolla tube and alternate with corolla lobes.
Ovary superior and syncarpous; usually 2–4 locules/lobes depending on lineage.
Fruit is most often a dry capsule with relatively few seeds.
exceptions: Cuscuta/dodders are leafless parasitic Convolvulaceae and break the normal leafy-twining-vine gestalt.
Corolla form varies from large funnels to smaller tubular or bell-shaped flowers.
Fruit is not always capsular across the entire family, though capsules dominate the local learner pattern.

Apocynaceae.confusion: Twining vines, milky sap and fused 5-part flowers can overlap.
Apocynaceae.tie_breaker: Convolvulaceae usually has alternate leaves + free persistent sepals + plicate corolla + capsule; Apocynaceae commonly has opposite/whorled leaves and very different gynoecium/follicle architecture.

Passifloraceae.confusion: Both may be vines with alternate leaves.
Passifloraceae.tie_breaker: Passiflora uses axillary tendrils and has a corona + elevated reproductive column with 3 stigmas; Convolvulaceae twines by its stem/petioles and lacks that Passiflora flower architecture.

Solanaceae.tie_breaker: Convolvulaceae typically has 5 free overlapping sepals and the conspicuously plicate/mid-banded corolla; Solanaceae usually has fused sepals and often many-seeded berry/capsule fruit.

learner_sequence: Is it a normal leafy plant or a parasitic Cuscuta-type exception?
Five free/persistent sepals behind the flower?
Corolla fused and visibly pleated/plicate or with 5 mid-petaline bands?
Superior ovary; later inspect the capsule and seeds.
Then move to genus/species characters: leaf shape, sepal shape/texture, pubescence, stigma form, capsule and seed.
